cells.tense: The satisfaction is here now while the pen is still in your hand.
cells.act: find the rhythm and stay in it
cells.ask: Whatever you're bringing forward, find the pace your own feeling will still be holding a month from now, and stay there this week. When the push to speed up shows, let it pass.
cells.core:
Where nothing has been chosen yet, the good version isn't a blank where a plan should be — it's room. What you imagine comes back full because you felt your way through it rather than counted it, which is why satisfied and busy don't look alike in you. Going well, work gets made at the speed your feeling can carry, and it holds.

The bend is that plenty invites the speed of everything at once. Find a pace your own feeling will still be holding a month from now for whatever you're bringing forward, and stay there; when the push to accelerate arrives, leave it alone. Steady outlasts fast when there's no finish line. Going slower than you could costs nothing here.
cells.sheetLine: There's plenty here, and it can wait for you to keep pace.
cells.verb: arriving at the deep, felt satisfaction of what was imagined all the way through
cells.place: the seed state where everything is possible and nothing has been chosen yet

cells.tense: The whole wide harvest is being hauled forward before any of it has ripened.
cells.ask: Take the possibility you're most braced about. Tend it once with a steady hand — one feeding, one look — then leave it be until it asks for you again.
cells.core:
Where nothing is chosen yet, the wide satisfaction starts being forced into arriving early. Good possibilities get tended all at once, checked twice, carried too close. You can feel the imagining being handled rather than grown. From across the room it reads as care; up close, the things in it are held too tight to get any bigger.

The bend is a grip. Take the possibility you're most braced about — the one you keep returning to out of fear it won't come through — and give it a steady hand and no clutching. One tending, then leave it be until it asks. Growth that had to be pressed isn't growth you keep. Let it arrive at its own size, in its own season.

cells.tense: A thing you imagined all the way through is over, and the door of it is behind you.
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: Carry what's finished and what's possible side by side this week, saying neither, choosing neither. See which one you keep returning to.
cells.core:
Nothing has been chosen here, and the last one happened at a door that is already shut. What was imagined got felt all the way to done, the door came down, and the standing there has gone on. From outside, the wide possibility still looks open. From where you are it doesn't, and no new thing gets taken up while the finished one is being stood beside.

What moves this isn't effort; it's holding. Carry two truths side by side — what's over and what's possible — and let neither be declared. Whatever you return to tells you what is still alive, and that is the material a next thing gets made out of, whenever you're ready to use it.
cells.sheetLine: The imagining finished. The door is shut behind it.

cells.tense: You bring imagined things to a felt finish and call it just how it goes.
cells.act: refine one distinction by close attention
cells.ask: Look closely at how you explain your best work to yourself, until you can tell the part that's true from the part that's habit.
cells.core:
Where everything is possible and nothing committed, you have a way of bringing imagined things all the way to a felt, finished satisfaction. It goes well enough that the results look like natural growth. They aren't. Someone kept the imagining fed until it could be felt in full, and stayed with the hard part of the craft while nobody watched, and that someone is you.

So look closely at how you explain the good outcome to yourself, and sort what's true in the explanation from what's habit. Naming the craft as yours changes what the next stretch is made of. It wasn't luck. It was attention, kept up on purpose, and you can keep it up on purpose again.
cells.sheetLine: Somebody kept feeding the vision. It was you.

attempts.check: The record never says the person is actually satisfied, only that abundant satisfaction is available at the outer face; the Too Much cell leans hardest here and could be read as asserting a mood the person hasn't got. A reader could also fairly say the Potential seat is being used to mean 'early days' when the record defines it as before differentiation, so every cell keeps the not-yet-chosen frame rather than a beginner frame. If my read is wrong, the asks still survive: pausing before speaking, tending one thing with a steady hand, and striking one line from a list teach something regardless of whether the status is real. The sentence that serves me is any line that makes the abundant fulfilment feel earned by the reader rather than by the person.
